A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SM-D, AIGTBench and OSM-Det study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original detector benchmarking, generalizability experiments, longitudinal social-media measurements, and linguistic, engagement and author analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds a training-data ablation and a reported analysis of Medium authors' AI-use disclosures.

M1.justification: OSM-Det remains LM-D fine-tuned on AIGTBench using Longformer-base-4096. The detection pipeline and generation prompts are unchanged. The new experiment evaluates an ablated training-data configuration without revising the proposed detector.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds the analysis task of checking Medium authors' AI-use disclosures. The platforms, training corpora, generation tasks and unseen-model/domain coverage remain unchanged. The new ablation reuses existing platform test coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same 14 detectors, including ConDA, GPTZero, CheckGPT and LM-D. The new control varies OSM-Det's training data; it does not introduce a distinct detection method. Newly cited security studies are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix J introduces an open-source-only training control that excludes the collected social-media subsets and evaluates on the existing platform test sets. Appendix I introduces syntax/keyword screening for disclosures. The original data split, preprocessing, detector settings and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix J tests the contribution of social-media training data through an ablation, while Appendix I adds a disclosure-compliance analysis. Generation-parameter sensitivity, unseen-model/domain tests, text-length analysis and linguistic case studies were already present in v2; moving generalizability into Section 5.2 does not add experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same Mann-Whitney U tests with p < 0.05 for engagement differences and retain the existing distribution displays. v3 adds no reported run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests for its new results.

E6.justification: v3 Table A2 adds ablated accuracy/F1 results: Medium 0.975/0.967, Quora 0.684/0.678 and Reddit 0.631/0.608. These are additional training-condition results; the full-model scores in Tables 2 and A6 remain unchanged. Appendix I newly reports 0.81% disclosure compliance, although its denominator is unspecified. Existing generalizability and social-media findings are retained.

T1.justification: The NTF definition in Equation 1 and the mathematical descriptions of the interpretation methods are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same research claims: systematic social-media quantification, construction of AIGTBench, selection of OSM-Det, differing platform trends and multidimensional content differences. The new public-access statement concerns reproducibility.

C2.justification: New Appendix I substantially expands interpretation with proposed mechanisms involving Reddit culture/moderation, technical-content structure, engagement psychology and author credibility, plus recommendations for platforms, creators and readers. These explanations are largely speculative. Appendix J interprets the ablation gap as missing social-media styles. The consolidated limitations also remove v2's categorical assurance that excluding early models cannot affect validity.

D1.justification: v3's abstract and footnote newly state that the project's code and dataset are public and provide a repository link. Existing prompts, preprocessing instructions, model configurations and hyperparameters remain unchanged. The disclosure analysis names syntax/keyword detection but supplies little implementation detail.

R1.justification: Section 2 briefly broadens its motivation to LLM vulnerabilities and hate speech, adding five references, including HateBench, PEFTGuard and CL-attack. The positioning against prior detection and monitoring research is retained. Publication updates and corrected Shapley-reference metadata concern existing works.

P1.justification: v2 Appendix H becomes v3 Section 5.2, and the interpretation-method appendix is renumbered. v3 adds discussion and ablation appendices, consolidates two coverage limitations, adds acknowledgements and makes limited wording edits. Most existing narrative remains verbatim.

P2.justification: v3 moves the model-composition chart and FPR/unseen-LLM tables into the main text, merges the existing Reddit vocabulary plot into Figure 5, adds an ablation table and widens Table A5. The redrawn Quora Integrated Gradients example removes an appended depression-related passage while retaining displayed logits. Most graphics are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new ablation provides direct evidence for the value of social-media training data, while project access information and the corrected Quora example improve reproducibility and clarity. These focused gains outweigh the limitations of the expanded discussion, whose speculative mechanisms and insufficiently documented 0.81% compliance claim provide weaker support.
